```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
source("labels.R")
root <- normalizePath("..")
release <- fread(file.path(root, "build/data/release.csv"))
funnel <- fread(file.path(root, "build/data/funnel.csv"))
checked <- fread(file.path(root, "build/data/validation_handcheck.csv"))
catalog <- fread(file.path(root, "data-raw/pg_catalog.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
setnames(catalog, c("pg_id", "type", "issued", "catalog_title", "language",
                    "catalog_authors", "subjects", "locc", "bookshelves"))
release[catalog, on = "pg_id",
        `:=`(subjects = i.subjects, locc = i.locc, bookshelves = i.bookshelves)]
release[, genre := assign_genre(bookshelves, subjects, locc)]
release[, model_period := assign_period(ht_year)]
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## What this report covers

This report describes the frozen automated release. It counts how books enter
and leave the build, summarizes the resulting collection, and reports the
publication-year validation. Nothing here changes `release.csv`. The manual
validation is an evaluation of the automated dates, not a set of corrections
applied back to individual books.

The counts describe this Project Gutenberg release. They do not estimate what
share of all historical publications had a given author or date.

## Selection

An eligible book is an English-language Project Gutenberg text with one named
personal author. The date comes from the earliest HathiTrust record matched on
normalized author surname and title. A book is released only when its author
also resolves through the Project Gutenberg agent identifier to a Wikidata
entity explicitly recorded as human, and the matched year falls within the
author's lifespan screen: no earlier than 15 years after birth, and no more
than five years after death. The lower bound of the release is 1700.

```{r funnel}
funnel[, decision := factor(decision, levels = decision)]
kable(funnel, col.names = c("Decision", "Books"), format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
ggplot(funnel, aes(decision, N)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Books", title = "Selection funnel") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

The release contains `r format(nrow(release), big.mark=",")` books. Most
exclusions are HathiTrust non-matches or authors who do not resolve to a
Wikidata human. The lifespan screen removes posthumous matches, implausibly
early dates, and books whose author has no usable lifespan.

## Dates and match quality

`ht_year` is the earliest year among the accepted HathiTrust matches. It is an
estimate of first publication, not a guarantee that the matched record is the
first edition. Later matched years are retained; their lower validation
accuracy is reported rather than used as an exclusion rule.

```{r dates}
ggplot(release, aes(ht_year)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 1700) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "HathiTrust matched year", y = "Books",
       title = "Matched publication years")
tier_counts <- release[, .N, .(tier = paste("Tier", tier))]
kable(tier_counts, col.names = c("Match tier", "Books"))
```

Tier 1 is an exact normalized title match within surname. Tier 2 allows a
normalized title to be a prefix of the other title, which mainly accommodates
subtitles. The collection is concentrated in the late nineteenth and early
twentieth centuries.

## Author metadata

Gender and country of citizenship are raw Wikidata claims, P21 and P27. They
are included as supplied by the 2026-10-21 Wikidata snapshot. Their coverage is
directly measurable; their accuracy against an independent biographical
authority is not. Birth and death years are retained from both Project
Gutenberg and Wikidata. When both sources supply a birth year and disagree,
`lifespan_conflict` records the disagreement without choosing a winner.

```{r authors}
authors <- unique(release, by = "agent")
coverage <- data.table(
  Field = c("Gender", "Country of citizenship", "Wikidata birth year",
            "Wikidata death year", "English author label"),
  Books = c(
    release[gender != "", .N],
    release[country_of_citizenship != "", .N],
    release[!is.na(wd_birth), .N],
    release[!is.na(wd_death), .N],
    release[wd_label != qid, .N]
  ),
  Authors = c(
    authors[gender != "", .N],
    authors[country_of_citizenship != "", .N],
    authors[!is.na(wd_birth), .N],
    authors[!is.na(wd_death), .N],
    authors[wd_label != qid, .N]
  )
)
coverage[, `Book coverage` := paste0(round(100 * Books / nrow(release), 1), "%")]
coverage[, `Author coverage` := paste0(round(100 * Authors / nrow(authors), 1), "%")]
kable(coverage[, .(Field, Books, `Book coverage`, Authors, `Author coverage`)],
      format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

both_birth <- authors[!is.na(birth) & !is.na(wd_birth)]
both_death <- authors[!is.na(death) & !is.na(wd_death)]
agreement <- data.table(
  Comparison = c("Birth year, exact", "Birth year, within one year",
                 "Death year, exact", "Death year, within one year"),
  Agreement = c(
    both_birth[birth == wd_birth, .N],
    both_birth[abs(birth - wd_birth) <= 1, .N],
    both_death[death == wd_death, .N],
    both_death[abs(death - wd_death) <= 1, .N]
  ),
  Compared = c(nrow(both_birth), nrow(both_birth), nrow(both_death), nrow(both_death))
)
agreement[, Percent := round(100 * Agreement / Compared, 1)]
kable(agreement,
      caption = "Agreement between Project Gutenberg and Wikidata. This is not independent accuracy.")
```

The release contains `r format(nrow(authors), big.mark=",")` distinct resolved
authors. Gender is nearly complete at book level, while citizenship is less
complete, especially among authors represented by few books. Exact lifespan
agreement is high where both sources have a year, but the roughly
`r format(release[lifespan_conflict == TRUE, .N], big.mark=",")`
flagged birth-year conflicts remain visible in the release.

```{r author-distribution}
per_author <- release[, .N, agent]
author_summary <- data.table(
  Statistic = c("Median books per author", "Mean books per author",
                "Authors with one book", "Books from the 100 most frequent authors"),
  Value = c(
    median(per_author$N),
    round(mean(per_author$N), 1),
    per_author[N == 1, .N],
    release[agent %in% per_author[order(-N)][1:100, agent], .N]
  )
)
kable(author_summary, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))

gender_counts <- release[, .N, .(gender = fifelse(gender == "", "missing", gender))]
gender_counts[, Percent := round(100 * N / sum(N), 1)]
kable(gender_counts[order(-N)], col.names = c("Wikidata gender claim", "Books", "Percent"))

top_cit <- release[country_of_citizenship != "" & !grepl(";", country_of_citizenship),
                   .N, country_of_citizenship][order(-N)][1:8, country_of_citizenship]
release[, citizenship_group := fcase(
  country_of_citizenship == "", "Missing",
  grepl(";", country_of_citizenship), "Multiple claims",
  country_of_citizenship %in% top_cit, country_of_citizenship,
  default = "Other single claim"
)]
cit <- release[, .N, citizenship_group][order(-N)]
cit[, Percent := round(100 * N / sum(N), 1)]
kable(cit, col.names = c("Citizenship group", "Books", "Percent"))
```

P27 preserves historical country names, so Britain is split across labels such
as “United Kingdom” and “United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland,” and
some authors have more than one citizenship claim. Those are reported as
recorded rather than collapsed into a modern nationality.

## Broad genre labels

The release itself has no single genre field. For description and the modeling
pilot, catalog metadata supplies four mutually exclusive labels. Fiction,
poetry, and drama require one unambiguous signal from Project Gutenberg
bookshelves, subjects, or the juvenile-literature LoC class PZ. Nonfiction
requires the absence of all three signals and a primary LoC class outside
literature. Books with conflicting creative signals, or literature-class books
without a specific signal, are excluded from genre analysis rather than forced
into a class.

```{r genre}
genre_counts <- release[, .N, genre][order(-N)]
genre_counts[, Percent := round(100 * N / sum(N), 1)]
kable(genre_counts, col.names = c("Genre label", "Books", "Percent"))
ggplot(genre_counts, aes(reorder(genre, N), N)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Books", title = "Deterministic broad genre labels")
```

## Publication-year validation

The validation sample contains 200 release books, stratified by matched period
and match tier, with a minimum of eight books per cell. The sampling weights
reconstruct the release composition. Each judged row has a cited
first-publication year in `validation_sourced.csv`. A date counts as accurate
when the HathiTrust year is within one year of that cited year. One book
remains ambiguous because its source edition cannot be identified, so it has
no verdict.

The reported estimate is stratified. Within each period-by-tier cell, accuracy
is the sample mean; cells are then combined in proportion to their size in the
full release. This prevents the intentionally oversampled early and late
periods from dominating the overall figure.

```{r validation}
checked[, year_ok := as.logical(year_ok)]
strat_est <- function(d) {
  N <- d[, .(N_h = weight[1] * .N), .(period, tier)]
  s <- d[!is.na(year_ok), .(n_h = .N, p_h = mean(year_ok)), .(period, tier)]
  s <- s[N, on = c("period", "tier"), nomatch = 0L]
  s[, W_h := N_h / sum(N_h)]
  p <- s[, sum(W_h * p_h)]
  se <- sqrt(s[n_h > 1, sum(W_h^2 * p_h * (1 - p_h) / (n_h - 1))])
  data.table(judged = sum(s$n_h), accuracy = p,
             low = max(0, p - 1.96 * se), high = min(1, p + 1.96 * se))
}
overall <- strat_est(checked)
overall_table <- overall[, .(
  Judged = judged,
  Accuracy = paste0(round(100 * accuracy, 1), "%"),
  `95% interval` = paste0(round(100 * low, 1), "% to ", round(100 * high, 1), "%")
)]
kable(overall_table, caption = "Weighted accuracy within one year")

by_period <- checked[!is.na(year_ok), .(
  Judged = .N,
  Accurate = sum(year_ok),
  Accuracy = paste0(round(100 * mean(year_ok), 1), "%")
), period]
kable(by_period, caption = "Unweighted accuracy inside each validation period")

judged <- checked[!is.na(true_year)]
judged[, gap := abs(ht_year - true_year)]
gap_table <- judged[, .(
  Books = .N,
  `Within 1 year` = paste0(round(100 * mean(gap <= 1), 1), "%"),
  `Within 5 years` = paste0(round(100 * mean(gap <= 5), 1), "%"),
  `Median absolute gap` = as.double(median(gap))
), period]
kable(gap_table, caption = "Absolute difference between matched and cited years")
```

Accuracy is fairly stable from 1850 through 1924 and weaker before 1850. The
1925-and-later cell is the clear failure point: the earliest available
HathiTrust match is often a reprint. That is why the release excludes the
whole stratum instead of trying to repair individual books.

The complete 200-row audit is written to `validation_audit.csv` beside this
report. It retains the cited year, source, and verdict separately from the
release.

```{r validation-table}
audit <- checked[, .(
  pg_id, period, tier, title = gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", title),
  authors, ht_year, true_year, year_ok, confidence, year_source, notes
)]
fwrite(audit, "validation_audit.csv")
kable(head(audit[, .(pg_id, period, title = substr(title, 1, 45),
                     ht_year, true_year, year_ok)], 12),
      caption = "First rows of the 200-book validation audit")
```
